task.description:
Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's §10 addition to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md (commit 3cfdaf7b on this branch) -- the ISS-0480 structural fix (a new Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 redirected to it via Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1 instead of calling Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) directly). Read §10 in full (sections 10.0-10.7, roughly lines 948-1679) plus §§0-9 for context on the design lineage and the reverted restore_sandbox mechanism this design must not resemble. Do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary as sufficient -- independently re-derive each of the following against the actual design text and, where a claim is checkable against real library source or arithmetic, against that source/arithmetic directly, per this project's 're-derive under the conditions the property is actually about' standard (core-directives.md).

SPECIFIC CLAIMS TO INDEPENDENTLY VERIFY, NOT TRUST:
1. The DBConnection.Ownership.Manager scoping claim -- that a Sandbox.mode/2 call issued against a SEPARATE Ecto.Repo (Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, its own pool/supervisor) cannot check in connections belonging to a DIFFERENT repo's (Letflow.Repo's) pool. Check this against actual Ecto/DBConnection source (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex and deps/db_connection, same standard ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis used) -- do not accept the design's own citation without opening the source yourself.
2. The pool-budget arithmetic in design section 10.2.2 -- the claimed connection counts (34 total at plain `mix test`, aggregate worst case 80 vs usable ceiling 97 at test_parallel.sh N=16) and the reconciliation against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's existing formula. Recompute independently from the design's own stated inputs; flag any arithmetic error found, however small.
3. That NO second Sandbox.mode/2 call is added anywhere against Letflow.Repo specifically -- grep/read the design's own normative section (10.3) for every Sandbox.mode/2 or put_dynamic_repo/1 call site it specifies, and confirm none of them targets Letflow.Repo in a way that reintroduces ISS-0113's reverted mechanism-4 (a second mid-test mode flip on the SAME repo the outer test already checked a connection out of).
4. That the design's own claim -- a narrow per-call-site conversion tranche cannot ever fully protect a file with zero TenantFixture involvement -- is actually argued, not merely asserted (design section 10.0). This determines whether ISS-0480 can be marked `resolved` (this design ships and works) vs. only ever `instrumented` (if the reasoning doesn't actually hold up) -- get this right, since ORCH's later status decision depends on your verdict here.
5. Public API/error-taxonomy preservation (design section 10.4) -- confirm provisioned_tenant!/1's @spec, opts() type and return shape are genuinely unchanged in the design's own normative section, and that none of the 46 existing call sites need any edit.
6. The regression-test mechanism in section 10.6 -- confirm it is genuinely deterministic (constructs the adversarial concurrent-caller scenario directly via Task.async, not suite-timing-dependent) and that it would plausibly fail pre-fix and pass post-fix as claimed, reasoning through the actual mechanism rather than taking the design's own claim at face value.

Apply the same FAIL discipline as any other gate: if any claim above does not hold up under your own re-derivation, this is a BLOCKER, named specifically (which claim, what you found instead), not a general impression. A PASS must state what you independently re-derived and how (per this project's own worked PASS example in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md), not merely 'looks correct.'

REGATE (rework iteration 1 for this gate): your original PASS above stood on §10.0-10.7 as they existed at the time and was correct for that content -- ELIXIR-DEV's real implementation then proved §10.0-10.7's core mechanism genuinely correct (172 tests passed, zero unexpected failures, including both actual ISS-0480 victims) but found that §10.4's 'zero call-site edits' claim was FALSE for 2 of 46 files (test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs), a gap your static read could not have caught. CODE-DESIGNER added a new §10.8 (and revised §10.4's claim to its true, narrowed scope) to close this gap -- read handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-02-code-designer.json's latest result.summary in full, then read §10.8 itself in the design document directly.

RE-GATE THIS SPECIFICALLY: (a) read test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs's hard_cleanup/1 (lines ~426-434) and test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs's provisioned_tenant/0 wrapper and its own async declaration (line 81) DIRECTLY yourself -- confirm §10.8.2.2's claim that this file is async: false (ORCH has already spot-checked this and confirms `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` at line 81, but re-derive it yourself rather than trusting ORCH's own spot-check) and therefore never scheduled concurrently with an async: true file, which is the entire safety argument for adding a bare Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call to an async:false file without it reintroducing ISS-0480's hazard. (b) Confirm §10.8.2.1's hard_cleanup/1 edit genuinely mirrors with_provisioning_repo/1's already-shipped shape (read that function in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex directly and compare). (c) Confirm §10.0-10.7 are textually unchanged (diff or direct comparison) -- the core mechanism must not have been reopened or weakened. (d) Confirm §10.8's two edits are specified precisely enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgement calls. State a fresh PASS/FAIL specifically for §10.8 and the revised §10.4 claim; your original 6-claim PASS for §10.0-10.7's core mechanism stands and does not need re-deriving from scratch (record it as prior gate history, not re-litigated).

result.summary:
REGATE (rework iteration 1) verdict: PASS on §10.8 and the revised §10.4 claim. The prior 6-claim PASS on §10.0-10.7's core mechanism (iteration 0, gated against commit 3cfdaf7b) stands unchanged -- see gate_history[0] -- and is not re-litigated here; it is independently confirmed below (point 3) to still apply verbatim, since §10.0-10.7's body is untouched by this rework.

(a) test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs genuinely async: false -- CONFIRMED by direct read, not inherited from ORCH's spot-check or the design's own citation. Grepped the file directly: line 81 is `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false`. Also read provisioned_tenant/0 (lines 113-118) directly: it is currently a bare, single-statement wrapper around `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` with no leading Sandbox.mode call today -- consistent with §10.8.2.2's premise that the proposed edit (one new leading `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` statement) is additive, not a revision of an existing call. Because this file's own moduledoc/use-declaration marks it async: false, ExUnit's own scheduling model (sync tests drained serially, never concurrently with an async: true file's checked-out connection) means a bare `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` call from this file's own test-support code cannot reach an async: true victim's connection -- the exact precondition the design's safety argument (mirroring §9.3/§9.4, independently confirmed correct at iteration 0) requires. Confirmed.

(b) §10.8.2.1's hard_cleanup/1 edit genuinely mirrors with_provisioning_repo/1's already-shipped shape -- CONFIRMED by direct read and side-by-side comparison, not accepted from the design's own claim. Current test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:291-301, with_provisioning_repo/1's actual body: `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto)` (line 292) -> `previous = Repo.get_dynamic_repo()` (line 293) -> `try do Repo.put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo); fun.() after Repo.put_dynamic_repo(previous) end` (lines 295-300). This is exactly the 4-step sequence §10.8.2.1 specifies for hard_cleanup/1's edit (mode call -> capture previous dynamic repo -> put_dynamic_repo(ProvisioningRepo) around the 3 existing Repo calls -> restore previous in an after block) -- the design's own numbered steps 1-4 are a verbatim structural match to the real, already-shipped helper, not a superficially-similar but different shape. Also independently re-read test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs:420-434 directly: broken_state_tenant!/1 (421) calls provisioned_tenant!(slug_prefix: ..., teardown: false) and registers on_exit(fn -> hard_cleanup(fixture.tenant_id) end) (422); hard_cleanup/1 (426-434) issues exactly the 3 bare Repo calls (DROP SCHEMA query, 2x Repo.delete_all) the design describes, with no wrapping of its own today -- matching the design's stated 'before' state precisely. Confirmed.

(c) §10.0-10.7 textually unchanged from iteration-0 gate -- CONFIRMED via `git diff 3cfdaf7b HEAD -- lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md` (3cfdaf7b is the exact commit iteration-0's gate_history entry cites as gated). Only 3 diff hunks exist in the entire file: (1) the top-of-file Status line, updated to describe the rework and explicitly state '§10 (through §10.7) is ... UNCHANGED by this rework except for §10.4's zero-call-site-edits claim'; (2) the single §10.4 bullet revised from an unqualified 'zero edits for all 46' claim to the narrowed, named-exception claim (44 of 46, 2 named files, pointing to §10.8); (3) an appended OQ-9 status paragraph at the tail of §10.7 plus the wholly new §10.8 section itself. No other line in §10.0-10.7's body (roughly lines 958-1491 and 1501-1677 of the current file) changed. This means every one of the 6 iteration-0 claims (DBConnection.Ownership.Manager per-repo scoping, pool-budget arithmetic, no second Sandbox.mode/2 against Letflow.Repo in §10.3, the narrow-conversion-cannot-protect argument, public API/46-call-site preservation, §10.6's deterministic regression-test mechanism) still holds against the current file exactly as it held at iteration 0 -- none of the text those claims were checked against moved. Confirmed.

(d) §10.8's two edits precisely specified enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgement calls -- CONFIRMED. §10.8.2.1 (tenant_fixture_test.exs): exact target function (hard_cleanup/1), exact 4 ordered steps (mode call with its own idempotency note, capture-previous, put_dynamic_repo wrap, after-block restore), an explicit statement of what is unchanged (the 3 existing Repo calls' content/order/target; broken_state_tenant!/1's own provisioned_tenant!/1 call; drop_table!/2; table_exists?/2) -- I independently confirmed this file has exactly the helpers named (hard_cleanup/1 at 426, drop_table!/2 at 436) with no ambiguity about which function receives the edit. §10.8.2.2 (promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs): exact target function (provisioned_tenant/0), exact single new leading statement (`Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`), an explicit, reasoned statement of what is NOT added (no after/restore, no put_dynamic_repo, and why each is correctly omitted), and an explicit statement of which 3 helpers are correctly left untouched (drop_schema!/1, schema_exists?/1, sandbox_process_definition_ids/1) with the mechanism distinction (SandboxPool vs TenantFixture provisioning) stated rather than asserted. Both edits are additions inside existing private-function bodies with no new module/config/file, matching what I independently verified of the current source. §10.8.4 additionally gives ELIXIR-DEV 4 concrete, numbered verification steps (exact pre-fix baseline counts: 14/14 and 12/12, the 172-test scoped re-run, mix compile clean) rather than leaving verification scope to implementer discretion. No ambiguity found in either edit's location, content, or ordering.

No BLOCKER found. §10.8 and the revised §10.4 claim are ready for ELIXIR-DEV to re-implement without further design clarification.
